policy.rule: Blanket 10-day window, one anchor. Every DATED, deletion-allowlisted artifact family keeps the run's anchor date and the 10 days before it; anything older is pruned via git rm in the daily auto-commit (forward commit — git history keeps every blob). Files NEWER than the anchor are never touched (backfill-safe). Scope is exactly mlb-backend/data_delivery/.
policy.anchor: MLB_END_DATE when the run sets it, else TODAY in America/New_York (master_pipeline Phase 6, zoneinfo DST-safe). One anchor for every window — the 2026-09-04 mix of an end_date-anchored 48h window with a UTC-anchored slate window is retired.
guardrails: Scope: only mlb-backend/data_delivery/ is ever touched.
The allowlist is asserted disjoint from the never-delete set (test_cleanup_fix).
Masters, records, and series readers are never deleted — see pressure_test below.

convention_reversal.note: DELIBERATE reversal of the repo's old 'committed artifacts are never auto-deleted' convention, applied ONLY to the ALLOWLISTED dated board-artifact families. Forward git rm commits only — git history keeps every blob. Masters, research/verdict records, and series readers remain never-delete and are asserted disjoint from the allowlist.
convention_reversal.scope: Formalized in retention_policy.py (FAMILY_POLICY) since 2026-09-04; Phase 6 derives every rule from that module — no family tuples are hard-coded in the pipeline.

pressure_test_2026_09_14.question: Does a blanket 10-day / MLB_END_DATE-anchored window break backend or frontend workflows?
pressure_test_2026_09_14.verdict: Safe — with the never-delete classes kept. The user's 'no files should have exemptions' clause was pressure-tested and the exemption classes survive on load-bearing grounds; every DATED board artifact rides the 10-day window exactly as specified.
findings: 10-day window: SAFE and an improvement — archive navigation (board date navigator, calibration history) extends from ~2-3 days to 10; all consumers are newest-only or board-backed, none read across a wide date range except the exempted series readers.

MLB_END_DATE anchoring: SAFE and fixes a latent inconsistency — the old code mixed an end_date-anchored 48h window with a UTC-anchored slate window; backfill runs (MLB_END_DATE in the past) previously could prune present-day artifacts. classify_artifact's anchor guard keeps anything dated AFTER the anchor regardless of windows.

No-exemptions clause: REJECTED for three load-bearing classes — (1) dateless masters: the daily pipeline CONSUMES lineups/batter_woba/team_woba parquets as runtime inputs and they carry no date to age (documented regression 42ef3f7: deleting lineups.parquet failed the pipeline loud); (2) game_level_features.csv feeds dashboard final scores and the RFE training frame; (3) mlb_feature_selection_state.json holds the adopted RFE serving width — silent deletion would silently revert model behavior. Series readers (run_engine_monitor_, pbp_defense_, pbp_chunks/, models/) fold ALL dated members — pruning resets rolling history or orphans cumulative stores.
Frontend impact: NONE negative — every frontend reader is newest-only or board-backed; a 10-day window only widens what the date navigator can reach.
Backend impact: NONE negative — Phase 6 still stages this run's artifacts first (seen-set), classifies via the pure predicate, and git-rms the remainder in a forward commit.
